subject.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these five named memory roles and per-agent role overrides as the durable public plugin and configuration contract?
rationale: The composition problem is real, but the patch permanently expands core configuration and the plugin SDK across bundled and third-party memory implementations; code review cannot determine the intended taxonomy, lifecycle ownership, or deprecation window without memory/plugin owner direction.

options.title: Sponsor the role contract
options.body: Approve the five-role taxonomy and per-agent overrides, require Doctor-only legacy migration, then refresh exact-final-head compatibility proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the first contract
options.body: Land only roles with implemented runtime protocols and defer speculative roles until concrete plugins and lifecycle contracts exist.

options.title: Settle the RFC first
options.body: Pause implementation review until the linked RFC confirms role names, ownership semantics, inheritance, and legacy migration policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the role contract
recommendation.body: Approve the five-role taxonomy and per-agent overrides, require Doctor-only legacy migration, then refresh exact-final-head compatibility proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects vincentkoc to plugin slot hardening, context-engine ownership, and the memory dreaming coexistence precedent closest to this decision.
